C:.comment: landing zone - downloads land here first, so it keeps the most free space

K:.comment: USB drive - takes from C:, pushes to D:, F:, G:, H: and J:. A source again as of 2026-10-06; it was held back because Windows was blaming this disk for errors that belonged to a different one. It logged 44,249 paging errors and 2,623 hardware I/O failures in September, so if it starts reporting errors again it will be held out of reads once more.

D:.comment: internal SATA - receives from C: and K:, fill to the brim, then cascades to F:, G:, H: and J:

F:.comment: USB 1TB - takes from C:, K: and D:, then pushes to G:, H: and J:. Was the parking lot until 2026-10-06, when it became a source again so the chain can reach J: at all.

G:.comment: internal NVMe - receives from C:, K:, D: and F:, fill to the brim, then cascades to H: and J:. Last in the chain, so it is the parking lot as a receiver; it still pushes outward to the exFAT volumes, which sit outside the chain.

H:.comment: USB 2TB exFAT - takes from C:, K:, D:, F: and G:, pushes to J:. A source again as of 2026-10-06; it was held back only because Windows blamed it for another disk's errors. Exempt from the 50% rule because exFAT reports slack.

J:.comment: 116 GB exFAT stick - end of the chain, small files only, still fill it, exempt from the 50% rule
